rationale: Economically coherent and internally consistent, but it is close to a mechanical crossing of two well-documented anomalies (R&D-capitalized book-to-market à la Park/Eisfeldt and asset turnover), so the marginal information beyond published intangible-value plus productivity screens is likely small.

This is essentially advertising-capitalized book-to-market times Novy-Marx gross profitability — two published anomalies multiplied — and the un-COALESCEd xad will restrict coverage to a small, consumer-tilted subsample, so any apparent alpha risks being a sparse-coverage artifact.

The denominator ADD(at, ADD(intan, gdwl)) double-counts intangibles and goodwill (both are already inside at, and gdwl is inside intan), so the expression does not compute the "intangible-inclusive asset base" the hypothesis describes, and the remaining content is just the known EBITDA/EV yield times turnover.

The sign logic is internally consistent, but the product reduces to mktcap × R&D-stock / sales², so the signal is dominated by 1/sales² scaling and extreme right-tail skew, making it largely a rediscovery of the price-to-sales value effect with a size/scale contaminant rather than a clean interaction.

The INDICATOR masks rather than interacts — every low-R&D firm, including genuine high-BM value stocks, is forced to zero and pooled into the short leg, so the portfolio sort mixes "expensive R&D firms" with "all non-R&D firms" and does not test the stated conditional hypothesis.

The "sales response per R&D dollar" leg is a genuinely novel productivity conditioner on cash-flow yield rather than a repackaged published anomaly, though the ratio can be negative and explodes for small MA(xrd), so winsorization or a log/rank transform of the second leg is needed before the result can be trusted.
